runs.text: Choosing how to keep the data is half the solution.
The group's contact list keeps, for each classmate, their
. New classmates join every year. You have to be able to
find someone's phone number by their name
how many have birthdays each month
How should the contact list be kept?

Draw three ways of keeping five contacts: three separate rows of cells, a row of cards with the three things together, and a list where you look up by name. Which one answers each question more easily?

The three separate rows force you to keep three lists aligned: if a name is added and the phone forgotten, everything shifts. The row of cards keeps each classmate's values together. The list by name finds a phone without walking through everything. And counting by month needs one more list, from month to amount.

entries.text: What goes in and what comes out?
The contacts and a name to search go in; a phone and a count per month come out.
The three separate rows are the parallel arrays of the kiosk till, in
Which parts does it split into?
You have to choose the shape of each piece of data according to the question it has to answer.
